title: Leveraging Telemedicine to Improve Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Use and Outcomes Among Rural Patients With Heart Failure
official: Leveraging Telemedicine to Improve Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Use and Outcomes Among Rural Patients With Heart Failure - the RURAL-HF Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a new way of adjusting heart failure medicines can improve health in adults with heart failure who live in rural areas. This study tests whether remotely helping local doctors safely raise these doses faster can improve health over the first 3 months after leaving the hospital.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the new approach help participants live longer, avoid needing a heart transplant or heart pump, stay out of the hospital for heart failure, and feel better day to day, over 6 months?
* Do more participants take all their recommended heart failure medicines, at the best doses, by 6 months?
* Does the new approach improve quality of life and daily activity, and how well does it work in everyday rural health care?

Participants will be placed by chance, like flipping a coin, into 1 of 2 groups: home monitoring alone or home monitoring plus medication optimization support. In the home monitoring alone group, participants' own doctors will manage their medicines as usual. In the medicine support group, heart failure specialists on the study team will use home readings and results from NT-proBNP blood tests, to send medicine advice to participants' own doctors. Researchers will compare the 2 groups to see if medicine support improves health and quality of life.

Participants will:

* Use a scale, blood pressure cuff, and activity tracker at home for 3 months
* May have routine blood tests ordered by their own doctor about 2 and 6 weeks after joining, if they are in the medicine support group
* Complete video or phone study visits when they join, at 3 months, and at 6 months
* Answer questions about their heart failure symptoms and quality of life at each visit
* Some participants may also be asked to take part in an interview about their experience.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age \> 18 years old
* Hospitalization for heart failure (HF) with intravenous diuretic use, with randomization within 14 days of discharge
* Residing in a rural area (home address in a rural area as defined by the Federal Office of Rural Health Policy)
* Established outpatient care (cardiology or primary care physician) at the participating sites
* Eligible to receive at least 2 of 4 guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes for HF with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF or HFmrEF; beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNi, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor), or at least 1 of 3 GDMT classes for HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF; ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNi, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor), and not on target doses of these medication classes
* Able to communicate with the study team via telephone or videoconference for study-related assessments and follow-up

Exclusion Criteria:

* Stage D HF under consideration for or a recipient of advanced HF therapies, including left ventricular assist device (LVAD), heart transplant, or inotrope therapy
* Discharge disposition to a nursing home, inpatient rehabilitation facility, or long-term care facility
* Potassium \> 5.5 mmol/L
* End-stage kidney disease or eGFR \< 25 mL/min/1.73 m²
* Inability to provide informed consent
* Pregnancy
